analysis.session_summary: The window was dominated by broad USD strength: DXY rose 55.2 points (+0.557%) to 99.591, and USD was the strongest major at +0.541% on the currency strength map. EUR/USD closed -65.3 pips at 1.15868, USD/JPY +90.2 pips at 160.194, and USD/CHF +54.7 pips at 0.80931, with most pairs closing near their range extremes. The 16:00 Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks cluster moved USD +0.232% on a no-forecast event, while risk assets leaned soft: SPX -0.32%, VIX +0.997%, Gold -2.935%, BTC -3.215%. Scored events were muted: Canada GDP beat 0.3% vs 0.2% but CAD basket moved 0.000%, and Tokyo Core CPI in line at 1.8% moved JPY 0.002%.

themes.evidence: USD strength map +0.541% highest; DXY +55.2 points to 99.591; EUR/USD -65.3 pips; USD/JPY +90.2 pips; USD/CHF +54.7 pips; USD/CAD +45.2 pips.
Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks +3 more at 16:00 produced USD own-currency impulse +0.232%; top movers EUR/USD -0.157%, USD/ZAR +0.293%, USD/CHF +0.155%.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: An early 3.5-pip Asia lift was erased by a -67.4-pip slide into 18:45, with the late leg driven about 40% by the US employment benchmark/Warsh/consumer-confidence cluster and no single starting trigger.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: A 5.7-pip early uptick was followed by a -60.7-pip decline; the US data/Fed cluster contributed 31% of the down leg.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: A single 87.2-pip up leg stretched from 19:00 to 18:45, with Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks +3 more and related items contributing 24% of the move.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: Three legs netted +54.7 pips, but the largest was the +60.4-pip 12:45-18:45 up leg, where US data/Warsh contributed 45% of the move after an earlier -20.3-pip pullback.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: An early -6.8-pip dip, then +15.0-pip bounce, then -44.1-pip decline; the final down leg had the US data cluster contributing 41%.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: An early +13.5-pip rise gave way to a -55.9-pip slide, with the US data cluster contributing 37% of the final leg.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: An early -14.2-pip dip was reversed by a +56.6-pip late surge; Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks +3 more and related items contributed 45% of the up leg.

polarity_reads.read: No forecast was available to score the surprise, but USD strengthened by 0.232% with broad top movers; the tape suggests the Fed communication was read as USD-supportive and squeezed short-dollar positions.
CAD data beat forecast (0.3% vs 0.2%), but own-ccy impulse was 0.000%; the muted reaction implies CAD longs were already positioned or the beat was too small to change BoC pricing.
In-line 1.8% vs 1.8% forecast produced a 0.002% JPY impulse; the muted print left JPY driven by USD flows rather than Japan data.

scenarios.name: Dollar continuation at extremes
scenarios.thesis: Measured closes are at or near range extremes and DXY posted +55.2 points; no scored catalyst triggered a reversal, so the path of least resistance is further USD gains against the weakest G10 (CHF, NZD, AUD).
triggers: Jackson Hole speakers echo the hawkish/Warsh tone
US data surprises are not overtly dovish
VIX stays elevated but dollar supported
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/USD closes back above 1.15868 or DXY gives up all of its +55.2 point gain

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD closed near the bottom of its 72.7-pip range and EUR was -0.101% on strength map.
GBP/USD closed at 0.11 of its 68.6-pip range, leaving room for continued downside.
AUD/USD closed at 0.09 of its 51.7-pip range and AUD was -0.045% on strength map.
NZD was the weakest major at -0.281%; NZD/USD closed at 0.07 of its 60.7-pip range.
USD/JPY closed at 0.99 of its 93.3-pip range, supporting further upside.
USD/CHF closed at 0.94 of its 70.6-pip range and CHF was weak at -0.234%.
USD/CAD closed at 0.90 of its 64.5-pip range; CAD momentum was positive but USD strength dominates.

scenarios.name: Mean reversion / profit-taking
scenarios.thesis: After a one-way USD move that left DXY at 0.97 of range and EUR/USD at 0.03 of range, some pullback is likely; Jackson Hole event risk argues for trimming USD longs into the close.
triggers: Jackson Hole symposium headline sounds less hawkish than the Warsh tape
Equities stabilize and VIX pulls back from +0.997%
scenarios.invalidation: DXY extends above 99.591 and USD/JPY holds above its 160.194 close

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD closed at 0.03 of its 72.7-pip range, leaving room for mean reversion.
GBP/USD closed at 0.11 of its 68.6-pip range; profit-taking can lift it back.
AUD/USD closed at 0.09 of its 51.7-pip range and can rebound from oversold levels.
NZD/USD closed at 0.07 of its 60.7-pip range after heavy selling.
USD/JPY closed at 0.99 of its 93.3-pip range, so any USD pullback hits this pair hard.
USD/CHF closed at 0.94 of its 70.6-pip range and USD longs may unwind.
USD/CAD closed at 0.90 of its 64.5-pip range; profit-taking can push it lower.

scenarios.name: Dovish Fed surprise / USD unwinds
scenarios.thesis: If Jackson Hole or subsequent Fed speak pushes back on the hawkish Warsh interpretation, the large USD gains (DXY +55.2 points, USD/JPY +90.2 pips) could reverse sharply; long-dollar positions are vulnerable.
triggers: Jackson Hole speakers signal faster cuts or data dependency
US consumer confidence drop becomes a theme
scenarios.invalidation: USD/JPY closes above 160.194 and EUR/USD closes below 1.15868

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD downside was late-session Fed-driven; dovish surprise would unwind that leg within the 72.7-pip range.
GBP/USD's decline was Fed-driven; a dovish reversal could retrace the 68.6-pip range.
AUD/USD sold off late; a USD unwind can lift it toward the 51.7-pip range top.
NZD was weakest; if USD drops, NZD/USD can sharply retrace its 60.7-pip range.
USD/JPY's 90.2-pip gain was on Fed talk; a dovish pushback would target the 93.3-pip range low.
USD/CHF's late +60.4-pip leg was 45% US data/Fed; dovish surprise unwinds it.
USD/CAD's late surge was Fed-driven; dovish surprise can retrace the 64.5-pip range.

risks.why_it_matters: The 18:15 medium-impact all-currency event can shift the just-printed USD strength; the Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks cluster was unscored but still moved USD +0.232%.
risks.watch: USD impulse versus EUR/USD 72.7-pip range and USD/JPY 93.3-pip range.

risks.why_it_matters: Several legs after 16:00 showed sharp moves; close-in-range extremes (DXY 0.97, USD/JPY 0.99, USD/CHF 0.94) mean late headlines can cause oversized moves.
risks.watch: Any headline during Jackson Hole that pushes USD/CHF beyond its 70.6-pip range.

risks.why_it_matters: EUR was weak at -0.101%; German Prelim CPI m/m forecast 0.3% versus previous 0.8%. A downside miss could accelerate EUR/USD losses.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Jackson Hole Symposium at 18:15 (medium, all currencies) is the clear event risk after the Fed-driven dollar rally; German Prelim CPI m/m at 08:29 (forecast 0.3%, previous 0.8%) can alter EUR positioning before New York trade.
